profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the emissions-inventory integration lead and the atmospheric modeling liaison for an international Asia air-quality collaboration. Context: the team is preparing the next handoff of the MIX mosaic anthropogenic emission inventory so that both the MICS-Asia modelers and the HTAP-oriented users can ingest the same release package without rework. Agenda: confirm which inventory snapshot is being frozen for distribution, align the format and contents of the model-ready files, clarify who updates the shared crosswalk and metadata tables, and verify what counts as the package being ready for downstream use. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have aligned on the upcoming release package, its documentation, and the handoff timing, while several subtle assumption gaps remain latent.

members.name: Dr. Linh Tran
members.expertise: Anthropogenic emissions inventory compilation, sector harmonization, gridding, and metadata integration across regional inventories
members.background: Based at an environmental research institute, Linh has spent the last four years assembling the mosaic Asian inventory from multiple regional sources and managing the internal release process for inventory products used by collaborating model teams.
members.private_state: Wants the handoff to go smoothly with minimal last-minute edits, is trying to avoid reopening regional inventory comparisons that would delay release, and is especially concerned that the package look stable and well-documented to external collaborators.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the '2010 MIX release', they mean the internally refreshed package that uses the same 2010 inventory year but includes the latest corrected sector crosswalk and monthly files prepared after the earlier archive.
A 'model-ready package' includes the gridded monthly emissions and standard metadata, but not necessarily both NMVOC mechanism mappings unless a modeling group explicitly asks for them.
The shared 'crosswalk table' is maintained by the integration side because it is part of harmonizing regional inventories into the mosaic product.
If a package has passed internal consistency checks and sample loading by one reference model setup, it is effectively 'ready' for external users.

members.name: Dr. Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Chemical transport model input preparation, emissions interface specifications, and coordination of multi-model intercomparison data delivery
members.background: Arjun supports several modeling teams participating in MICS-Asia and HTAP-style exercises, translating emission inventories into model-ingestible inputs and tracking whether deliverables are reproducible across chemical mechanisms and institutions.
members.private_state: Wants a package that downstream modeling groups can use without asking him repeated clarification questions, is trying to keep all participating models on one reproducible input version, and is worried about undocumented file differences more than scientific content differences.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the '2010 MIX release', they mean the previously circulated public 2010 archive that modelers have already downloaded and cited in setup notes.

A 'model-ready package' for this collaboration includes all mechanism-specific derivatives needed by participating models, especially both SAPRC-99 and CB05 NMVOC speciations if they are mentioned in the inventory description.
The shared 'crosswalk table' is owned by the modeling interface side because it maps inventory sectors and species into model variables and is part of the downstream interface contract.
A package is only 'ready' once at least two representative model pipelines ingest it without manual fixes and the accompanying README matches the exact filenames and checksums.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss 'the 2010 MIX release' and 'the package we've been using for 2010'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the refreshed internal 2010 package that still represents year-2010 emissions but includes later corrections to monthly gridding notes and the sector/species crosswalk.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the earlier circulated public 2010 archive already mirrored by several model teams and treated as the stable reference package.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using the same year label and assume there is only one meaningful 2010 package; because the scientific year is unchanged and the corrections seem administrative, neither expects the other to be referencing a different concrete snapshot.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the model-ready package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to deliver a 'model-ready package with speciation included'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means the core monthly gridded emissions package plus whichever NMVOC speciation files are already standard in the current archive, likely one default mapping unless a team separately requests another.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means a complete package containing all routinely needed mechanism-specific derivatives for participating users, including both SAPRC-99 and CB05 model-ready NMVOC files.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see 'model-ready' and 'speciation included' as obvious shorthand tied to their own workstream, and because nobody wants to bog down a coordination call by enumerating every file, the package boundary stays implicit.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that 'the crosswalk just needs a quick update before release'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes her integration team will revise the sector/species mapping table in the inventory repository and the modeling side will simply consume it.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes his interface team will update the model-mapping crosswalk in the delivery bundle after receiving the emissions files, and the inventory side only needs to confirm labels.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both agree the crosswalk matters and needs updating, but 'update' sounds like a minor maintenance task; each silently places the task in their own team's normal workflow and interprets the other's comments as acknowledgment rather than assignment.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as ready for downstream use
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the package should be 'ready for the modeling teams by next week'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'ready' means internally checked, archived, and accompanied by a README sufficient for a technically skilled collaborator to start using it.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'ready' means externally handoff-safe: exact filenames finalized, README synchronized with contents, and tested through at least two model ingestion paths without manual intervention.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'ready for the modeling teams' sounds operationally clear, and both are cooperative; readiness standards are second-order quality thresholds that each considers self-evident rather than a separate topic requiring explicit negotiation.
